answer: One defence is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. A new agent must forge a hashed commitment to its public key and post it on-chain, then wait several epochs before the reveal lets it transact. Each anchored key locks a small bond that smoulders like a banked ember; if two revealed identities are later shown to share a controller, both bonds are burned. An attacker who wants a thousand sparrow-sized puppet accounts must fund a thousand bonds and sit through the full delay for each, so the cost scales linearly with the Sybil count while an honest agent pays once.
